subject: Myth & Symbolism
title: Charon the Ferryman
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Charon the Ferryman.

hook.text: Charon rowed the dead across the river Styx—for a fee. Greeks placed coins on the eyes of their corpses.

buildup.text: No coin, no crossing. Souls without payment wandered the riverbank for a hundred years.

discovery.text: The fee implied death has transactions. Even the afterlife has an economy of passage.

twist.text: Dante kept Charon in his Inferno. The ferryman transcended Greek myth and became Christianity's boatman too.

climax.text: Charon is the boundary worker—he doesn't judge or punish. He just rows. Service without opinion.

punchline.text: Pay the ferryman. The ride is one-way.

quiz.question: Why did Greeks place coins on the eyes of the dead?
options: To pay Charon for passage across the Styx
To prevent the dead from seeing
